title: News feed
summary: Fan-out on write for most users, fan-out on read for celebrities.

lesson.problem: Users follow hundreds of accounts and open their feed many times a day. Building it on every request means querying every account they follow.
why: Fan-out on write (push): when someone posts, workers copy the post ID into the precomputed timeline of each follower. Reading a feed becomes a single, fast cache lookup.
Fan-out on read (pull): store each post once and assemble the feed when it is opened. Writing is cheap, but reading is slow and expensive.
Push breaks for celebrities: one post would trigger millions of timeline writes. Real systems use a hybrid: push for regular accounts, pull for celebrity posts, merged when the feed is read.
takeaways: Choose where to pay the cost: at write time or at read time.
Feeds are read far more than posts are written, so precomputing usually wins.
Handle outliers (very popular accounts) with a separate path.
